A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Markovian language-modeling work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of sections.

before.justification: v5 reports original training and evaluation results on fifteen-term addition, GSM8K, and Wikipedia, including perturbation analyses, cross-model evaluations, and generated examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and reports a revised perturbation comparison using answer prediction with and without the original question.

M1.justification: The proposed question-to-CoT-to-answer bottleneck, frozen predictor, trainable LoRA state update, and TEI/PG/PPO objectives remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and revised length descriptions do not establish a different proposed algorithm; question access is introduced as an evaluation control.

E1.justification: Addition, GSM8K, and Wikipedia coverage is retained. Section 5.4 adds an input-availability scenario in which the answer predictor receives the original question alongside the CoT. Human evaluation and multi-turn tasks remain unevaluated.

E2.justification: The fragility comparison changes its reference from untrained CoTs to prediction conditioned on the original question plus the same CoT. This introduces an inference-time comparator, without reporting a separately trained question-plus-CoT model. The TEI/PG/PPO comparisons and cross-model evaluator membership are retained; DeepSeek-R1 remains discussion only.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 replaces the trained-versus-untrained perturbation metric with m2, which contrasts perturbation-induced log-probability losses under question absence and presence. This substantially changes the control and measurement supporting the causal-reliance claim. Sections 4.1 and 5.2 also revise fixed-length descriptions to maximum-length CoTs, including up to 150 tokens, without establishing that retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The central fragility analysis is redesigned to test dependence on question availability rather than comparing trained and untrained CoTs. Wikipedia back truncation disappears from Figure 4, leaving deletion, front truncation, and character replacement. Appendix A retains arithmetic truncation analyses, and the qualitative cases in Appendices C and E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix G newly states that every experimental configuration used four independent runs. This is additional run-count reporting, not evidence of increased replication, and conflicts with retained captions reporting three GSM8K runs and six Wikipedia cross-model runs. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces the earlier trained-minus-untrained sensitivity results with new question-availability difference curves, materially changing the empirical evidence for causal reliance. These measure a different quantity and cannot establish same-setting performance gains. Other results remain unchanged, including Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6, GSM8K accuracy of 35.94% versus 69.14% in the best run, and Wikipedia accuracy of 8.2% versus 10.5%.

T1.justification: Section 5.4 introduces the distinct mathematical definition of m2 in Equation 3 and removes the earlier derivation connecting complete perturbation to the informativeness reward. The core MLM definition and reward equations remain unchanged. Footnote 2 also adds an F-coalgebra characterization, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and four contribution statements retain the same substantive claims: informative Markovian CoTs, the 33.2-percentage-point GSM8K improvement, perturbation sensitivity, and cross-model transfer. The new introductory emphasis elaborates the existing causal-bottleneck claim.

C2.justification: v6 explicitly interprets its revised fragility metric as separating causal dependence from improved accuracy, replacing v5's trained-versus-untrained interpretation and complete-perturbation explanation. The limitations concerning human interpretability, multi-turn applicability, and serial-generation cost remain substantively intact despite condensation. Section 5.3 still describes the old Figure 4 comparison, creating an interpretive inconsistency.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds RunPod usage, approximately five hours per H100 training run, 180 GPU-hours for reported experiments, and approximately $30,000 in overall project compute costs. Conversely, v6 removes the explicit repository link and the temperature-2.0 sampling disclosure. The missing link does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning beyond CoT approaches to information-theoretic communication, RNNs, S4, Mamba, Kalman filters, and probabilistic latent-state models. Nine newly cited works support these connections and the policy-gradient discussion. Existing CoT references are largely retained; the expansion changes the conceptual comparison with prior architectures.

P1.justification: v6 expands introductory and formalism explanations while condensing the GSM8K, interpretability, and discussion passages. Future Work is folded into Section 6, Impact and Reproducibility move to Appendices F and G, acknowledgements disappear, and references move after the appendices. This constitutes substantial narrative and structural reorganization.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column layout with a redesigned author block and broadly resized and repositioned figures. Figure 4 changes from four panels to three, with new axes, legends, trajectories, and caption. Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6 retain their underlying graphics despite relocation and scaling.

improvement.justification: The question-present control in Section 5.4 provides more targeted evidence of CoT dependence than v5's trained-versus-untrained contrast, whose complete-perturbation case reduces to the informativeness reward. Expanded explanations and research positioning also improve accessibility. These gains are moderated by documentation regressions: removal of the repository link and sampling temperature, inconsistent run counts in Appendix G, and Section 5.3's outdated description of Figure 4. Overall, the evidential and explanatory gains support a modest improvement.
